messages:
anya: FYI ticket INC-4597 — customer reports wrong tool executed after we roll out a rename with tenant prefixes. They call `acme:summarize` but backend returns outputs that match the old legacy summarizer. Posting logs and repro below.

sam: Can you paste a minimal repro request (headers + body)? also which deployment (hosted/dedicated/private)?

anya: Hosted. Customer provided this request (sanitized):
```
POST /v1/toolcall HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx
X-Tenant: acme
Content-Type: application/json

{"tool": "acme:summarize", "args": {"text": "...long doc..."}}
```
Response body: 200, `{"status":"ok","result":"[legacy style summary]"}`. They expected the v2 model's style.

anya: Attached router logs:
```
[router] 2132109876 GET /tool/resolve acme:summarize -> tool_uuid=98a7f2 (legacy_summarize) cached=true age=120s
[registry] alias acme:summarize -> 3b4c1d (summarize-v2) (updated 2132109500)
```

leo: Hmm registry shows alias points to v2 (uuid 3b4c1d) but router cache has 98a7f2. That smells like cache TTL + rollout race. Did we do a staggered registry rollout earlier?

deploy-bot: Config rollout 2f9d6ac deployed 2132109300 by sam — included tenant-prefix alias migration (global -> tenant-scoped)

sam: We did staggered rollout exactly 15–30m ago. Router caches have default alias TTL=300s. If the registry changed while some routers still had old entries they could happily serve legacy uuid until TTL expiry.

anya: Customer reports it persisted even after 10 minutes. Their app is behind a single router in us-east-1.

sam: Two follow-ups: 1) can you ask them to retry with header `X-Registry-Cache-Control: force-refresh` (we added a temporary hook to bypass router cache) and 2) paste the exact tool string they used (case matters).

anya: They retried with force-refresh and now get v2 output. They used `acme:Summarize` (capital S) in original call.

leo: Ah — case-folding + tenant prefix interaction. Our registry canonicalizes aliases to lowercase at write-time but some older router clients used case-sensitive matching. When we rolled the tenant-scoped alias migration we created both `acme:summarize` (lowercase) and left older `acme:Summarize` cached on older routers. That explains why force-refresh fixed it.

sam: Good catch. Short-term mitigation: tell customers to use lowercase handles or call with full tool UUID. I'll also trigger an immediate cache invalidation for the affected router (us-east-1 node id r-us-17).

leo: Medium-term fix: normalize alias lookup to NFKC lowercase in the router and backfill normalized keys to router caches during rollout. I'll open a PR to canonicalize at lookup layer and add a backfill job that pushes normalized aliases to all routers.

anya: Customer-facing message draft: "We identified a cache + naming edge case after a rename/tenant migration. If you can retry with header `X-Registry-Cache-Control: force-refresh` or use the full tool UUID we will serve the updated tool. We are invalidating caches and deploying a permanent fix." Want me to send?

sam: Yes send it. Also add that any customers hitting odd outputs should contact support and include the raw request + `x-router-id` response header.

leo: Action items:
- leo: PR for canonicalized lookup + backfill (ETA today EOD).
- sam: invalidate router cache r-us-17 and monitor (doing now).
- anya: notify customer and confirm resolution.

deploy-bot: Router cache invalidation job started for r-us-17 (job id ci-7741)

sam: Cache invalidation completed for r-us-17. Will watch metrics for misrouted toolcalls for 30m.

anya: Customer confirmed after retry they get v2 summary. Marking customer resolved but leaving thread open until leo's PR lands.

leo: I'll keep this thread updated. PR link when ready: https://git.redwood.ai/infra/router/pulls/432 (WIP).

anya: thanks team :white_check_mark: 

sam: adding postmortem stub in #postmortems once we close ops tasks.

leo: quick note for SRE — consider reducing alias TTL to 60s during big rollouts or add a propagation fence to avoid this window.

anya: noted. Closing customer loop now.
